predecessors.name: Later Liang
predecessors.text: the Jingnan circuit round Jingzhou (Jiangling), held by Gao Jichang, 'a former general of Liang'

successors.name: Song dynasty (Northern and Southern Song)
successors.text: the Jingnan realm, overrun in 963: 'When the Song army was passing through the Jingnan, it easily took control of the capital city of Jingnan, Jiangling'

ledger.x: 924: the Gao family's Jingnan, or Nanping, begins at Jingzhou.
963: the Song take Jiangling without a fight.

wars.name: Song conquest of Jingnan and Wuping
wars.outcome: Song troops sent after the Wuping rebellion of 962 passed through Jingnan, took Jiangling in 963 and received Gao Jichong's surrender; the country was 'overrun ... with little resistance'.

certainty.note: The state is known by its capital Jingzhou and Cliopatria's outline; no page gives prefectures or a frontier with the Later Tang, Ma Chu, the Later Shu or the Southern Tang.
